name: Nebraska

agency.name: Nebraska Department of Labor, Labor Standards

rates2026.note: New in July 2026; NDOL wage sheet says July 17, 2026, the minimum wage chart says July 18, 2026

rates2026.area: Training wage, new employees aged 16-19, first 90 days (not seasonal/migrant)

rates2027.note: Per NDOL minimum wage chart updated 2026-07-31 (then $15.53 in 2028, $15.80 in 2029, $16.08 in 2030)

minWage.smallEmployer: State minimum wage applies to employers of four or more persons; smaller employers fall under the federal FLSA only if covered by it.

tipped.note: Cash wage plus tips must reach the applicable minimum wage

minWage.other: Student learners in bona fide vocational training: at least 75% of the minimum wage. From July 2026: optional youth wage ($13.50, ages 14-15) and 90-day training wage ($13.50, ages 16-19).

overtime.note: No state overtime requirement: overtime is claimable under state law only if agreed; otherwise federal FLSA (over 40 hours/week) applies.

source.quote: Overtime wages can be claimed under the Nebraska Wage Payment and Collection Act only if those overtime wages were previously agreed to by the employer and employee.

sickLeave.accrual: 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (after 80 hours of consecutive employment)
sickLeave.capNote: 20+ employees: 56 h/year; 11-19 employees: 40 h/year; employers with fewer than 11 employees are not covered. Unlimited carryover but use can be capped at 40/56 h; no payout at separation unless combined PTO.
sickLeave.note: Nebraska Healthy Families and Workplaces Act (2024 ballot initiative), as amended in 2025 to exempt employers with fewer than 11 employees. Excludes under-16s and seasonal/temporary agricultural workers.

source.quote: The Nebraska Healthy Families and Workplaces Act applies to employers with 11 or more employees.

finalPay.fired: next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner
finalPay.quit: next regular payday or within two weeks, whichever is sooner
finalPay.ptoNote: Earned but unused vacation/PTO must be paid at separation (vacation itself is optional). Sick time under the HFWA is not paid out unless combined into PTO.

source.quote: Nebraska law requires that final wages be paid on the next regular pay day or within two weeks of the termination, whichever is sooner.

ptoSource.quote: Earned but unused vacation / PTO time is due to the employee upon separation of employment.

breaks.meal: 30 consecutive minutes per 8-hour shift, only in mechanical establishments, workshops and assembling plants

source.quote: Only mechanical establishments, workshops, and assembling plants are required to provide a 30 consecutive minute meal break in each 8-hour shift to employees.

rightToWorkSource.quote: No person shall be denied employment because of membership in or affiliation with, or resignation or expulsion from a labor organization or because of refusal to join

notes.text: From July 2026, employers may pay 14- and 15-year-olds a youth minimum wage of $13.50, and new hires aged 16-19 a training wage for their first 90 days.

source.quote: Beginning July 18, 2026, an employer may pay a youth minimum wage of $13.50 per hour to employees who are 14 or 15 years of age.

notes.text: The minimum wage rises to $15.26 on January 1, 2027, then $15.53 (2028), $15.80 (2029) and $16.08 (2030), per NDOL's updated chart.
Paid sick time (voter-approved in 2024) took effect October 1, 2025, but only for employers with 11 or more employees.

source.quote: Nebraska Healthy Families and Workplaces Act takes effect October 1, 2025.

uncertain: dol.nebraska.gov and nebraskalegislature.gov refused all connections on 2026-10-11 (curl, WebFetch and Chrome). All Nebraska sources were read from Internet Archive (web.archive.org) copies of the official NDOL/Legislature URLs, captured in 2026 (Paid Sick Time FAQ snapshot 2026-08-31, revised Oct 31, 2025; minimum wage chart updated 7/31/2026; Wages sheet version 7/17/2026). Re-check on the live site.
Youth/training wage start date: NDOL minimum wage chart says July 18, 2026; NDOL Wages sheet says July 17, 2026.

The 2026 bill that set the $15.26 (2027) rate and youth/training wages was not identified by number; values taken from NDOL's chart. The NDOL FAQ PDF used for final pay still showed the 2025 rate ($13.50), so it is an older document; final-pay rule confirmed by the 7/17/2026 Wages sheet.
